subject: Civil Engineering
title: Buttress Dams
description: A quick, practical guide to Buttress Dams.

hook.text: A flat wall can't hold back a river alone — but lean supports on the downstream side can.

buildup.text: Buttress dams have a thin upstream face supported by triangular walls — buttresses — behind.

discovery.text: They use 30-50% less concrete than gravity dams — the buttresses transfer loads efficiently.

twist.text: Each buttress works independently — damage to one doesn't compromise the entire structure.

climax.text: Daniel-Johnson Dam in Canada — the world's largest multiple-arch buttress dam.

punchline.text: A thin wall with strong legs — buttress dams trade mass for smart engineering.

quiz.question: What advantage do buttress dams have over gravity dams?
options: They can be built in wider valleys with weaker rock foundations
They use 30-50% less concrete by using triangular supports instead of solid mass
They generate more hydroelectric power due to increased water flow

details.summary: Buttress dams use a series of triangular supports, called buttresses, on the downstream face to brace a thin upstream wall or slab against water pressure. By replacing solid mass with structural frames, they use 30 to 60% less concrete than gravity dams while maintaining comparable height capacity.
details.whyItMatters: Buttress dams offer material savings in locations where concrete is expensive or aggregate sources are limited, though their complex formwork and construction offset some material savings.
takeaways: Triangular buttresses brace a thin upstream face against water pressure
They use 30 to 60% less concrete than equivalent gravity dams
Complex formwork for buttresses increases labor cost compared to gravity dams

faq.question: What are the different types of buttress dams?
faq.answer: Flat slab buttress dams have a continuous concrete slab supported by evenly spaced buttresses. Multiple arch buttress dams replace the flat slab with a series of small arches spanning between buttresses.

faq.question: Why are buttress dams less common today than in the past?
faq.answer: Modern roller-compacted concrete construction makes gravity dams faster and cheaper to build, reducing the material savings advantage of buttress dams. Buttress dams require complex formwork and skilled labor.
